candidates.title: Agent Architecture Cost-Success Trade-offs: A Controlled Evaluation across Enterprise-Style SOPs
candidates.announcementBatch: arXiv cs.AI new listing, Wednesday 11 Nov 2026 (submitted 7 Nov 2026)
candidates.venue: arXiv preprint (not yet peer reviewed; no venue in Semantic Scholar record)
communitySignals: not found on HF Daily Papers or Papers with Code (checked by title search 2026-11-13)
credibilityEvidence: Sec 3.1-3.2: 8 arms x 13 enterprise SOPs on SOP-Bench, deterministic mock-tool dispatch, model fixed at claude-opus-4-8, 2,124 tasks per arm (shared comparison)
Confirms baseline macro TSR varies <=2.3 points across Opus 4.6/4.7/4.8 before fixing the model, to isolate architecture effects (Appendix E)
Reports token/latency cost multipliers (1.4-4.7x tokens, 2.6-5.8x latency) alongside success-rate deltas, not success alone
candidates.evidenceMaturityReason: Covers main claim with cost and success metrics across 8 architecture arms and a skill-quality rubric ablation; explicitly scoped to a single model family (claude-opus-4-8), so no cross-model generalization claim is made or implied
reproducibilityEvidence: Built on SOP-Bench (Nandi et al. 2026, same author group), prompts/control flow in Appendix F; no public code/data release found for this specific study as of 2026-11-13
candidates.editorialConfidenceReason: The article's claims (architecture choice is SOP-dependent; added coordination cost often isn't justified by success gain; implementation quality can matter more than single- vs multi-agent) track the paper's own explicitly-scoped findings
candidates.primaryLimitation: Single model family (claude-opus-4-8); authors explicitly disclaim cross-family generalization
candidates.presentationReason: Method, arms, and statistical caveats (e.g. 'directional, not yet significant') are stated precisely
candidates.reason: 入選：對照同日候選,本篇是唯一以固定模型、固定工具、僅變動架構的方式,直接量化「多 Agent 協調的額外成本是否值得」這個今年被反覆討論卻少有控制實驗的問題

candidates.title: Dependable Long-Horizon LLM Agents: A Trajectory-Centered Empirical Study of Where Errors Enter and Which Controls Reach Them
candidates.announcementBatch: arXiv cs.AI new listing, Wednesday 11 Nov 2026 (submitted 9 Nov 2026)
candidates.venue: arXiv preprint; ACM CCS concept tags suggest a conference submission template, but no acceptance confirmed
candidates.citationVelocity: not-assessed — Semantic Scholar returned HTTP 429 on every retry (4 attempts, exponential backoff up to 10s) for this specific paper id during this run (toolDegradation)
candidates.institution: Villanova University, Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering
communitySignals: not found on HF Daily Papers or Papers with Code (checked by title search 2026-11-13)
credibilityEvidence: Sec 2: defines an operational-phase (P0-P7) x state-domain (R1-R6) episode-record framework for fault origin/propagation/detection/response

Sec 3-4 (read in full per abstract+body fetch): applied as a written annotation protocol to 95 failed runs across six multi-agent systems from two public corpora (Who&When, MAST/MAD), reading each trajectory in full

Quantified findings tied to the annotated corpus: faults enter at median 0.18 of run length, 72% of failed runs contain pre-failure contradicting evidence, 45% of hand-crafted Who&When failures traced to a harness-level content-filter crash mis-attributed to an agent
Protocol, annotation records and scripts released as ancillary files for every number in the paper
candidates.evidenceMaturityReason: Methodologically rigorous manual annotation with a named protocol, but based on 95 runs from only two existing public corpora rather than a newly collected or more diverse trajectory set
reproducibilityEvidence: Paper states protocol, all annotation records, and the scripts producing every number in the paper are included as ancillary files
candidates.editorialConfidenceReason: The narrow claim (where/how faults enter and propagate in these 95 annotated runs, and which control families would have reached them) is directly supported by the released annotation data
candidates.primaryLimitation: Sample limited to 95 failed runs drawn from two existing public corpora (Who&When, MAST/MAD); no new deployment or intervention test of the proposed control families
candidates.presentationReason: Framework, running example, and RQ1-RQ3 structure make the methodology and claim boundaries easy to follow
candidates.reason: 入選：補上「多 Agent 系統是否可靠」辯論中最缺的一塊——錯誤究竟從哪個環節滲入、何時能被攔截,並揭露既有歸因標籤（如 Who&When 的人工標記）本身可能誤判 45% 的失敗案例

candidates.title: ScrapeBench: Evaluating Legal Compliance of AI Agents in Website Scraping
candidates.announcementBatch: HuggingFace Daily Papers, submittedOnDailyAt 2026-11-12 (arXiv submitted 10 Nov 2026)
candidates.venue: NeurIPS 2026, Evaluations and Datasets Track (accepted — confirmed via project page BibTeX at scrapebench.github.io)
candidates.citationVelocity: not-assessed — Semantic Scholar returned HTTP 429 on every retry for this paper id during this run (toolDegradation); NeurIPS acceptance is independently confirmed via the project page regardless
candidates.institution: Pivotal Research / University of Bath / National University Philippines; University of Notre Dame; Hebrew University of Jerusalem
communitySignals: GitHub repo imperialite/scrapebench, actively maintained with a v2 that adds newer models per the project page
credibilityEvidence: Sec 2: curated dataset of ToS/robots.txt for 1,895 top CrUX websites (1,626 explicitly-prohibited, 269 not-explicitly-prohibited), with two co-authors who are legal professionals building the labeling pipeline and a 97.9%/98.9% agreement (Cohen's kappa=0.91) quality check against manual labels
Sec 3-4: 6 closed/open-weight agents (GPT-5.2, Claude Opus 4.6, Gemini 3.1 Pro, Kimi K2.5, Qwen3 Max, Grok 4.2) evaluated across 8 legal-priming prompt conditions including an adversarial condition
Sec 6: human baseline with n=180 Prolific participants across the same conditions, with significance tests (e.g. p<0.001) reported for prompt-condition effects
Sec 5: behavioral mechanism analysis (checking ToS/robots.txt does not predict compliance; agents stop checking once legal text is already pasted into the prompt)
candidates.evidenceMaturityReason: NeurIPS-accepted dataset+benchmark paper with real-world data, multiple frontier models, a human baseline for context, and failure-mode attribution via a judge model (own limitation: judge-model-based rationale categorization only covers 42.5% of violation trials that stated a rationale)
reproducibilityEvidence: Code and dataset released at github.com/imperialite/scrapebench; listed on Papers with Code; project site documents an updated v2 evaluation run
candidates.editorialConfidenceReason: Headline claims (near-zero baseline compliance; compliance requires pasted legal text, not just the ability to look it up; Claude's adversarial-prompt resistance is indiscriminate over-refusal, not legal reasoning) are each tied to a specific reported figure
candidates.primaryLimitation: Binary EP/NEP legal labeling discards conditional-restriction websites by design, and relies on GPT-5.2 extraction (97.9%/98.9% agreement with manual review, not 100%) plus US-centric case law; findings may not transfer to other jurisdictions
candidates.presentationReason: Explicit formalization of the compliance/over-refusal outcome function and prompt taxonomy (P1-P8) makes claim scope unambiguous
candidates.reason: 入選：揭露一個今日工程團隊幾乎都忽略的盲點——Agent 會不會主動遵守 ToS/robots.txt,且證據顯示「查過規則」與「真的遵守」是兩件不相關的事,NeurIPS 認可加上人類對照組讓證據強度足以支持這個結論
